title: If you want to own the stock, buy it instead of selling a cash-secured put
summary: A cash-secured put harvests the volatility risk premium and takes on delta risk. The speaker says if you already want to own the stock, selling puts is often a poor deal: you are not paid enough for the upside you give up if the stock rallies without you.

steps.caption: Buy the stock: full upside if the stock you like rallies.
Sell the $95 put: you keep only the premium if the stock rises.
The gap on the right is the upside you sold for the premium.
Below the strike both positions lose almost the same: the put carries most of the stock's downside.
If you want to own it, the missed rally is the real cost of waiting.

takeaways: A short put earns the volatility risk premium and carries delta risk.
If you really want the stock, the upside you give up may cost more than the premium.
Sell puts when the premium is rich, not just to get a lower entry.
caveats: The transcript gives no numbers; the strike and volatility are illustrative.
